brief.situation: 21:00 in a medical ICU. You are Mr. Novak's nurse. He is 64, ten days after chemotherapy for lymphoma, admitted yesterday for atrial fibrillation with a fast rate, now controlled. He says he feels cold and shaky; the monitor shows a temperature of 38.4 C.
handover: Lines: an implanted chest port, accessed, and one peripheral IV.
This morning's blood count posted at noon and has not been reviewed.

Unit policy for fever in a patient after chemotherapy: two sets of blood cultures (peripheral and port), call the intensivist, and the first dose of the ordered broad-spectrum antibiotic within 60 minutes of the fever. A PRN acetaminophen order is in place.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time; study pace runs three simulated minutes per real minute. Pause any time.
Each assessment takes the time on its button. Decide what the findings mean, what to stop or start, and who must know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

why.question: How severe is his neutropenia, what does the fever mean, and how fast must you act?

parts.label: Grade and meaning
parts.criteria: ANC under 500 is severe (under 100 profound); a single temperature of 38.3 C or more with an ANC under 1,500 is neutropenic fever, an emergency because infection spreads without the usual signs.
parts.modelAnswer: His ANC is about 180, so severe neutropenia. A temperature of 38.4 with that count is neutropenic fever, and it's an emergency.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Calls now; two sets of cultures (peripheral and port) before the antibiotic; the broad-spectrum antibiotic within 1 hour of the fever; precautions; acetaminophen does not replace or delay any of it.
parts.modelAnswer: Call the intensivist now, draw two sets of cultures, one from the port, and get the antibiotic in within the hour. Acetaminophen doesn't buy time; it just hides the fever. Put precautions in place.

scoring.modelReasoning: Ten days after chemotherapy his ANC is about 180: severe neutropenia (under 500). A single temperature of 38.3 C or more with an ANC under 1,500 is neutropenic fever, and it is an emergency because infection spreads fast without the usual signs. Call the intensivist now, draw two sets of blood cultures (peripheral and port), give the broad-spectrum antibiotic within 1 hour of the fever, and put precautions in place. Acetaminophen and a recheck later only hide the fever and lose time.

ancQ.ask: While you assess: which ANC is severe neutropenia?
ancQ.explain: Severe neutropenia is an ANC under 500; profound is under 100.
